rubriker.title: Bodhana Sivanandan joins strong field in Salamanca
rubriker._rss_content: The Salamanca Chess Festival will take place from 10 to 14 November, bringing together six players for a rapid round-robin tournament. The field includes 11-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan (pictured), former world top-ten player Loek van Wely and Spanish grandmaster Paco Vallejo, who returns to top-level competition after a lengthy absence. Elisabeth Paehtz, José Martínez Alcántara and Anastasiia Hnatyshyn complete the lineup. Several side events are also scheduled. | Photo: Nils Rohde / ChessBase

rubriker.title: Bodhana Sivanandan jugará el Magistral de Salamanca junto a Vallejo y Van Wely
rubriker._rss_content: El Festival de Ajedrez de Salamanca se celebrará del 10 al 14 de noviembre y reunirá a seis jugadores en un torneo rápido por sistema de liga. Entre los participantes figuran Bodhana Sivanandan (en la imagen), de 11 años, el exintegrante del top 10 mundial Loek van Wely y el gran maestro español Paco Vallejo, que regresa a la alta competición tras una ausencia prolongada. Elisabeth Paehtz, José Martínez Alcántara y Anastasiia Hnatyshyn completan la nómina de participantes. También están previstas varias actividades paralelas. | Foto: Nils Rohde / ChessBase

Bavarian Championship: Four players finish tied for first, Sasikiran claims title on tiebreaks
rubriker._rss_content: Indian grandmaster Krishnan Sasikiran won the Bavarian Chess Championship in Gmund am Tegernsee, finishing on 7½/9 points and taking first place on tiebreaks. German GMs Frederik Svane and Roven Vogel finished second and third, while Indian FM Arun Daakshin also reached 7½ points. All four won their final-round games with the black pieces, bringing an event that attracted 548 participants to a close. | Photo: Sandra Schmidt

rubriker.title: Yu Yangyi retains Chinese Rapid Championship title after Armageddon decider
rubriker._rss_content: Yu Yangyi successfully defended his Chinese Rapid Championship title in Shaoxing, defeating 18-year-old Xiao Tong in an Armageddon decider after six games had failed to separate the finalists. Xiao had previously eliminated Ding Liren and Lu Shanglei in blitz tiebreaks to reach the final. Meanwhile, Lu secured third place by defeating Xu Xiangyu. | Photo: Chinese Chess Association

rubriker.title: Aaron Nimzowitsch: 140 years since the birth of a chess pioneer
rubriker._rss_content: Born in Latvia, Aaron Nimzowitsch was one of the most important players and theorists of the first third of the 20th century, influencing generations of chess players with his strategic ideas. His life, however, was far from easy and sadly cut short. Today marks the 140th anniversary of his birth. | Photo: J. Graudenz

rubriker.title: The young king faces his toughest challenge
rubriker._rss_content: Gukesh Dommaraju will defend his world title against Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva after a remarkable rise that made him the youngest undisputed champion in history. Since his 2024 triumph, however, the Indian grandmaster has endured a more difficult period and slipped down the world rankings. The match therefore presents a different challenge: rediscovering his best form while facing a younger rival who arrives with strong recent results and considerable momentum. | Image: FIDE

Vinneren avga bare et Les mer

rubriker._rss_content: Nord-Østerdal sjakklubb arrangerte Desperados Grand Prix i Alvdal 7-8. november 2026. Det ble omspill for å kåre vinneren, og her gikk Kittilsen seirende ut. Tredjeplass gikk til Ivan Les mer

rubriker._rss_content: England’s Amaya Agarwal, 11, scored 5/9 in the girls U20 World Junior Rapid in Al Ain and won the $500 best under-12 prize.
